title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
technique: speculative decoding for large-batch long-context serving using draft models with sparse (StreamingLLM/SnapKV) KV cache; theoretical model to choose drafting strategy and speculation length

optimized_metrics.evidence: Can we simultaneously improve throughput and latency without sacrificing accuracy, particularly for long sequences?
Can we simultaneously improve throughput and latency without sacrificing accuracy, particularly for long sequences?
enhance throughput and reduce latency without compromising accuracy (lossless verification)

headline_claim.text: For moderate to long sequences, we demonstrate up to 2.51x speedup for LLaMA-3.1-8B when serving batch sizes ranging from 32 to 256 on various types of hardware and tasks.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 6, Tables 1-2 (T_AR vs T_SD, speedup x); Fig 1b per-token latency
Fig 1b throughput tokens/s vs per-token latency

metric_definitions.term_as_written: expected latency per token for SD
metric_definitions.definition_quote: Hence, the expected latency per token for speculative decoding is simply T_Avg = T_Total^SD / Omega(gamma,alpha).
metric_definitions.notes: T_Total^SD = gamma*T_D(B,S) + T_V(B,S,gamma); Omega = expected generated tokens per step = (1-alpha^(gamma+1))/(1-alpha). This is per decoding step latency for the whole batch (per-token of each sequence), not system tokens/s

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The speedup of speculative decoding ... T_Avg^SD / T_T = (1/Omega(gamma,alpha)) * (gamma*T_D/T_T + T_V(gamma)/T_T)
metric_definitions.notes: Tables report x = T_AR / T_SD (ratio of autoregressive to speculative per-token latency, ms). Because every sequence in a fixed batch advances at the same rate, a latency speedup at fixed batch size equals a throughput speedup; paper equates them ("speedup ... demonstrating speculative decoding's ability to improve throughput")

load_regime: fixed batch size sweep (B=1..256, notably 32-256), fixed sequence lengths 256-100k, offline generation of 96 tokens per sequence, greedy; no request arrivals
tradeoff_acknowledged: Conventional trade-off (SD speedup falls with batch size for short sequences, where compute-bound verification dominates) is acknowledged: below a critical sequence length SD slows down at large batch (Fig. 6). Drafting KV budget trades draft cost vs acceptance rate.
extractor_notes: Title says 'latency-throughput tradeoff' but the experiments are fixed-batch decode steps; 'throughput' and 'latency' improve together because batch fixed. No TTFT, no SLO, no request-rate load; speedup reported is per-token latency ratio. Table units (ms) inferred: T_SD=(gamma*T_D+T_V)/Omega matches table values.
load_class_quote: Each run generates 96 tokens per sentence in the batch through greedy decoding on 20 batches. (§5.1 setup)
